newsitem.title: GERMANY: German union boss says investment needed for jobs.
newsitem.headline: German union boss says investment needed for jobs.

text.p: Klaus Zwickel, the head of powerful German engineering union IG Metall, on Thursday called for a European investment programme to combat stubbornly high unemployment rates.

Speaking at a conference on European monetary union, Zwickel said the new employment chapter of the Maastricht treaty provides the necessary conditions for job-creating investment and urged the EMU project not be delayed beyond its planned 1999 start.
Zwickel, saying European nations spend around 400 billion marks on unemployment benefits, said it was "high time" that new jobs were created.
He said European nations also needed to coordinate economic strategies regarding traffic and information technologies, the environment and energy.
In addition, Zwickel said the euro would help relieve pressure on wages in Europe and create greater transparency in wage costs and prices.
Zwickel said delaying the euro would lead to instability in financial markets which could lead to job losses.
